cohort: 100 participants between the first and seventh day after delivery in an obstetric ward.
finding: Portable handheld-ultrasound devices show near-perfect agreement and correlation with standard ultrasound devices for estimating post-void residual volume and diagnosing postpartum urinary retention, with 100% agreement for covert postpartum urinary retention.
mod_finding: Subgroup analyses, including mode of delivery, did not show a significant difference in agreement and correlation rates between the ultrasound devices.
cross-section timing: Between the first and seventh day after delivery
